title: New Novaspace forecast: 6,500+ EO satellites to launch by 2035
summary: A forecast by Novaspace predicts over 6,500 Earth observation satellites will launch by 2035, generating $155.9 billion in manufacturing revenue. The expansion is driven by governments increasing sovereign intelligence and surveillance capabilities.

title: Elve qualifies millimeter-wave amplifiers for spaceflight
summary: Elve, a California startup, has qualified its 100-watt millimeter-wave Traveling Wave Tube Amplifier platform for spaceflight. The qualification was supported by U.S. Space Force Small Business Innovation Research funding.

title: What’s next for ISR in space
summary: A panel of experts discusses the future of Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) in space, highlighting its evolving role and upcoming advancements.

title: Moog Highlights Huntsville Expansion and New Hardware-in-the-Loop Lab During Space and Missile Defense Symposium
summary: Moog Inc. announced a major expansion of its Huntsville, AL facility, including a new secure Hypersonic/Interceptor Hardware-in-the-Loop (HWIL) lab. The announcement was made during the Space and Missile Defense Symposium.

title: Rock West Composites® Is Premiering Its New STRATOPultrusion™ Product Line at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference
summary: Rock West Composites is introducing its new STRATOPultrusion™ product line at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference in Salt Lake City. The space-grade composite materials are designed for small satellite applications.

title: LatConnect 60 selects Transcelestial’s Space Optical Network for SWIRSAT imaging constellation
summary: LatConnect 60 has partnered with Transcelestial to integrate an optical communications terminal on its SWIRSAT-1 mission, leveraging Transcelestial's Space Optical Network for the SWIRSAT imaging constellation.

title: Draper Selects Proteus Space for Advanced On-Orbit Mission
summary: Draper selected Proteus Space for an advanced on-orbit mission. Proteus Space, a dual-use aerospace company, will provide rapid, end-to-end access to space for the mission.

title: Moog Inc. Expands METEORITE Satellite Bus Capacity for High-Maneuverability Missions
summary: Moog Inc. has expanded the capacity of its METEORITE satellite bus to support high-maneuverability missions. The expansion enhances the platform's capabilities for precision motion and control systems in space applications.

title: Eoptic, Inc. Selected to Supply DeepScan™ Imaging Payloads Scheduled for Launch in 2027
summary: Eoptic, Inc. has been chosen to supply DeepScan™ imaging payloads for a mission scheduled to launch in 2027. The company, based in Rochester, NY, specializes in advanced multi-spectral and multi-modal imaging systems.

title: The 77th International Astronautical Congress (IAC 2026) is the One Space Event You Cannot Miss
summary: The 77th International Astronautical Congress (IAC 2026) is highlighted as a must-attend event for the global space community. The IAC has been a key annual gathering for over 75 years.

title: Launching 10,000 tiny 'femtosats' to Saturn? NASA funds 18 futuristic spaceflight ideas
summary: NASA has selected 18 futuristic spaceflight concepts for its Innovative Advanced Concepts awards, including a proposal to launch 10,000 tiny 'femtosats' to Saturn. The awards aim to support out-of-the-box ideas for advanced research.

title: How will NASA's astronaut training hub change with commercial space stations?
summary: NASA's astronaut training hub at Johnson Space Center is evolving to incorporate commercial space stations, reflecting growing collaboration between NASA and private industry in human spaceflight. A recent tour highlighted ongoing efforts to integrate these new partnerships into existing training programs.

title: 'We Want to Believe' book explores the reality of UFOs: 'It's always going to be more likely that someone is wrong about what they saw' (interview)
summary: A book titled 'We Want to Believe' by Adam Kirsch examines the human fascination with UFOs, suggesting skepticism about reported sightings. The literary critic discusses the cultural and psychological factors behind belief in unidentified aerial phenomena.

title: This Week In Space podcast: Episode 224 — The Science of Artemis
summary: The latest episode of the 'This Week In Space' podcast discusses the science behind NASA's Artemis Program's lunar exploration plans, featuring guest Dr. David Kring. The episode explores the objectives, strategies, and scientific goals of the Artemis missions.

title: SpaceX sends 27 Starlink satellites to orbit on 100th Falcon rocket launch of the year (video, photos)
summary: SpaceX successfully launched 27 Starlink satellites into orbit from California on August 22, marking the 100th Falcon rocket mission of the year.

title: On this day in space! Aug. 22, 1963: X-15 sets world altitude record
summary: On August 22, 1963, U.S. Air Force Captain Joe Walker set a world altitude record by flying an X-15 rocket plane higher than any pilot had previously achieved.

title: What happens when a galaxy's supermassive black hole turns off? These dying radio galaxies could show us
summary: Astronomers discovered a new population of galaxies with fading radio lobes, showing what happens when a galaxy's supermassive black hole stops fueling them. This reveals the evolution of dying radio galaxies.

title: Trump signs new national space policy to enable 1,000 US rocket launches per year
summary: The U.S. has updated its national space policy under Trump to enable over 1,000 rocket launches annually by 2030, aiming to boost the nation's spaceflight and reentry capabilities.

title: 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' cast talks losing sleep, living up to their character's legacy, and learning to ride a horse for season 4 (interview)
summary: The cast of 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' discusses the challenges of long hours, high expectations, and learning new skills like horseback riding for season 4.

title: Ship 41 Completes Engine Testing Ahead of Flight 14
summary: Ship 41 has completed engine testing in preparation for Flight 14, while Ship 40 is being transported back to Starbase from Christmas Island.

title: Stoke Space conducts second stage fit checks, completes first stage engines ahead of Nova debut
summary: Stoke Space has completed second stage fit checks and first stage engine assembly for its Nova rocket, aiming for a debut launch around 2026. The company is advancing its fully reusable vehicle as competition in the space industry intensifies.

title: Zhuque-3 Completes Second Flight with Successful First-Stage Landing
summary: Zhuque-3, a methalox rocket developed by LandSpace, successfully completed its second flight and achieved a first-stage landing. This milestone marks a significant advancement for the company in reusable rocket technology.

title: Ship 40 arrives at Christmas Island, Plans Return to Starbase
summary: SpaceX has successfully guided Starship Ship 40 to a location near Christmas Island. The company plans to return the vehicle to Starbase for further operations.

title: Launch Preview: Chang’e 7 headlines week of Chinese and Starlink launches
summary: China is preparing for the Chang'e 7 mission following a recent launch failure, while SpaceX's Starlink launches also dominate the week's space activities.

title: Firefly promote next block of Alpha amid Eclipse progress
summary: Firefly Aerospace is advancing the development of its next-generation medium-lift rocket while also making progress on its Eclipse program. The company is promoting its upcoming Alpha rocket block amid these developments.

title: Blue Origin overviews plan for dual pad ops at Cape Canaveral
summary: Blue Origin is planning dual launch pad operations at Cape Canaveral as it restores its primary launch pad at LC-36A. The company has shared details about its operational expansion at the site.

title: Rocket Lab advances via series of announcements
summary: Rocket Lab has established a new subsidiary in Germany and introduced a containerized mobile launch system. These moves mark the company's expansion and innovation in launch capabilities.

title: Amid failure, Wenchang celebrates milestone as China launches AI satellites and prepares for lunar south pole mission
summary: China's Wenchang Space Launch Site celebrated its 50th launch milestone while also experiencing a failure. The site launched AI satellites and is preparing for a lunar south pole mission.

title: Starbase Production lining up future vehicles
summary: SpaceX's Starbase production site is advancing the assembly of multiple Starship vehicles. This indicates ongoing preparations for future missions and testing at the facility.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates its 50th anniversary by releasing a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements over the past five decades. The publication underscores the agency's contributions to space exploration and technology.

title: Phoenix 3: concept study for a reusable European spacecraft
summary: Engineers from ESA and industry partners completed a concept study for Phoenix 3, a reusable spacecraft for microgravity experiments and Earth return.

title: Proba-3’s eclipse hours before totality in Europe
summary: Proba-3 mission will create an artificial solar eclipse to study the Sun's corona just hours before the total solar eclipse in Europe. The mission is a collaboration between ESA and other partners.

title: A double eclipse for Proba-3
summary: Proba-3 mission observed a double eclipse involving the Moon crossing its field of view. This event highlights the mission's precision in solar observation.

title: How ESA mimics and models the 2026 total solar eclipse
summary: ESA is preparing to study the 2026 total solar eclipse by using artificial eclipse missions and computer simulations to observe the Sun's corona. This approach allows scientists to gather more data than a natural eclipse would permit.

title: Your chance to run software in deep space on ESA's asteroid mission
summary: The European Space Agency is inviting European researchers and companies to test their software aboard the Hera mission, which will travel millions of kilometers into deep space. This presents a unique opportunity for in-flight testing of innovative software in a real deep-space environment.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time using a drone at ESTEC, the European Space Agency’s technical centre in the Netherlands. This marks a transition from drone flight to sounding rocket applications.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will use two satellites to create an artificial solar eclipse, allowing the coronagraph to study the Sun's corona by blocking out the bright solar disk. The mission demonstrates advanced formation flying and precision alignment in space.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event will showcase innovative space startups and foster collaboration with Europe's space industry on September 16-17 at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands.

title: Letara Raises ¥2.6B to Build its Hybrid Rocket Engine Tech
summary: Japanese propulsion startup Letara raised ¥2.6 billion ($16 million) in a pre-Series A funding round to develop its low-cost hybrid rocket engine technology.

title: SpaceWERX Announces 2026 STRATFI Awardees
summary: Space Force announced the newest awardees of the SpaceWERX Strategic Funding Increase (STRATFI) program during the Fed Supernova conference. The awards were revealed as part of efforts to advance space technology and innovation.

title: Op-ed: The Technologies That Could Define the Future of Space
summary: Daniel Biedermann of NewSpace Capital discusses key technologies shaping the future of space. The op-ed highlights emerging trends in the space industry.

title: Muon Space Raises $250M Series C
summary: Muon Space secured $250 million in a Series C funding round to enhance its satellite production capacity and expand mission capabilities.

title: Portal Books Dedicated Falcon 9 Amid Constrained Launch Market
summary: Portal Books a dedicated Falcon 9 launch amid a constrained space launch market. The company is partnering with Maverick Space Systems to sell excess fairing capacity for rideshare opportunities.

title: SpaceX’s Mobile Ambitions: Build, Partner, or Buy?
summary: SpaceX is exploring strategies to compete with major telecom providers like AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon by expanding into mobile services. The company aims to leverage its satellite and launch capabilities to tap into a multi-billion-dollar revenue opportunity.

title: White House Publishes S&T Strategy for National Security
summary: The White House, through the Office of Science and Technology Policy, released a new National Security Science & Technology Strategy. This strategy aims to guide national security efforts through scientific and technological advancements.

title: Zeno Power Books its First Nuclear Mission to the Moon
summary: Zeno Power has secured its first commercial payload agreement with Firefly Aerospace to send a nuclear-powered heating unit to the Moon on a mission launching no earlier than 2028. The mission, part of Firefly's CS-8 CLPS mission, aims to demonstrate Zeno's technology for maintaining power in lunar conditions.

title: Deep Dive: FY27 Defense Space Budget
summary: The U.S. Space Force's FY27 budget request has been announced at a record $71.3 billion. This significant funding highlights the growing emphasis on defense space initiatives.

title: Slingshot’s Portal Adds New AI-Powered Missions
summary: Slingshot Aerospace has enhanced its Portal platform with AI-powered capabilities to improve monitoring of the increasingly crowded space environment. The update aims to assist operators in managing satellite traffic and space debris more effectively.

title: Fireside Chat with German Space Command: Featuring Major General Michael Traut
summary: A fireside chat featured Major General Michael Traut, Commander of the German Space Command, discussing Germany's military space operations and efforts to protect space assets. The event highlighted the integration of space capabilities into national defense strategies.

title: White House Targets Support for 1,000 Launches Per Year by 2030
summary: The White House announced a goal to support over 1,000 launches and reentries annually by 2030 through a new National Security Presidential Memorandum. This initiative aims to boost U.S. space industry capabilities.

title: The Evolution of the Space Edge With Voyager CTO Paul Tilghman
summary: The article discusses the evolution of spaceborne computing, focusing on the 'space edge' rather than orbital data centers. It features insights from Voyager Space's CTO, Paul Tilghman, on this emerging trend.

title: Starcloud Adds $250M to Series A at a $2.3B Valuation
summary: Orbital data center startup Starcloud raised an additional $250 million for its Series A round, increasing its valuation to $2.3 billion. The funding was led by Manhattan West.

title: Space Norway Appoints Rune Jensen as Acting CEO With Morten Tengs Departure
summary: Space Norway has appointed Rune Jensen as Acting CEO following Morten Tengs' departure at the end of August. The company will now search for a permanent CEO.

title: Sypris Electronics Wins Manufacturing Deal to Support LEO Constellation
summary: Sypris Electronics has secured a manufacturing contract to produce power processing units for an unnamed Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellation. The deal marks a significant expansion in the company's involvement in next-generation satellite technology.

title: Muon Space Raises $250M Series C to Build Large-Scale Constellations
summary: Muon Space secured $250 million in a Series C funding round to expand its large-scale satellite constellations and enhance mission capabilities. This investment marks a significant milestone in the company's growth and development.

title: Phantom Space Names Worth Wray as COO
summary: Phantom Space has appointed Worth Wray as its chief operating officer to oversee day-to-day operations, efficiency, and business scaling. The move aims to support the company's growth as it ramps up activities.

title: Rocket Lab Launches SAR Satellite for Japan’s iQPS
summary: Rocket Lab successfully launched a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite for Japan's iQPS on August 21 from New Zealand. This marks Rocket Lab's ninth mission supporting iQPS's satellite constellation.

title: Rocket Lab’s Bold Move to Acquire Iridium: Analysts Break Down the Strategy
summary: Rocket Lab announced plans to acquire Iridium in a major move within the satellite sector. Analysts are dissecting the strategic implications of this acquisition.
